label: prf:x5-z5-automorphism
title: Proof of x5 z5 automorphism
html:
Invariance of the defining equation:

  y^2  =  (\zeta_5 x)^5 - 1
      =  \zeta_5^{\,5}\, x^5 - 1
      =  x^5 - 1,

using \zeta_5^{\,5} = 1. So \phi_5 sends points of \mathcal{X}_5 to points of \mathcal{X}_5. Iteration gives \phi_5^{\,k}(x, y) = (\zeta_5^{\,k} x, y), and \phi_5^{\,5} = \mathrm{id} because \zeta_5^{\,5} = 1. Order 5: if \phi_5^{\,k} = \mathrm{id} then \zeta_5^{\,k} x = x at the point (2, \sqrt{31}), forcing \zeta_5^{\,k} = 1, and hence 5 \mid k because \zeta_5 = e^{2\pi i/5} is a primitive fifth root of unity. The map is bijective with inverse \phi_5^{\,4}, and both are polynomial, so \phi_5 is an automorphism of the affine curve; it extends to the smooth projective model, fixing the single point at infinity. \square
